Ben More.about: The highest mountain in the National Park, a huge steep cone above Crianlarich.

routes.name: Benmore Farm
routes.text: From Benmore Farm on the A85, a relentless climb up the north-west shoulder: almost all ascent and no respite.

routes.name: With Stob Binnein
routes.text: Down to the Bealach-eadar-dhà Bheinn and up Stob Binnein, returning down Benmore Glen.

Stob Binnein.about: Ben More's twin, with a distinctive cone that looks sliced off at the top.

routes.name: Inverlochlarig
routes.text: From the road end in Balquhidder Glen, up the south ridge over Stob Coire an Lochain.

routes.name: From Ben More
routes.text: Down to the bealach between them and up the steep north ridge.

Ben Lui.about: One of the finest Munros: a great north-east corrie, Coire Gaothach, often holding snow into spring.

routes.name: Glen Cononish
routes.text: From Dalrigh near Tyndrum, the track up Glen Cononish past the gold mine (rideable to the end), then into Coire Gaothach and up its north-east ridge.

routes.name: Glen Lochy
routes.text: Shorter but wetter: from the A85, cross the river and the railway, then up the forest and Fionn Choirein.

Cruach Ardrain.about: A complex hill of ridges and corries south of Crianlarich, with Beinn Tulaichean as its southern top.

routes.name: Crianlarich
routes.text: From the A82, through the forest and up the Grey Height ridge over Meall Dhamh.

routes.name: Inverlochlarig via Beinn Tulaichean
routes.text: From Balquhidder Glen, up the grassy south ridge over Beinn Tulaichean.

Ben Oss.credit: John Knight from Clackmannanshire, Scotland, CC BY 2.0
Ben Oss.about: A shapely peak between Ben Lui and Beinn Dubhchraig, above Loch Oss.

routes.name: Dalrigh with Beinn Dubhchraig
routes.text: From Dalrigh, through the Caledonian pinewood of Coille Coire Chuilc and up Beinn Dubhchraig, then over the bealach to Ben Oss.

Beinn Ìme.about: The highest of the Arrochar Alps, a bulky hill above the Rest and Be Thankful.

routes.name: Succoth via Bealach a' Mhàim
routes.text: From the head of Loch Long, the Cobbler path into the corrie, then over Bealach a' Mhàim and up the south-east slopes.

routes.name: Butterbridge
routes.text: Short and steep from Glen Kinglas on the A83.

An Caisteal.credit: Mick Knapton at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0
An Caisteal.about: 'The castle': a rocky summit at the head of Glen Falloch, reached by the long north ridge of Twistin Hill.

routes.name: Glen Falloch via Twistin Hill
routes.text: From the A82 south of Crianlarich, under the railway, up Sròn Gharbh and along Twistin Hill. Often climbed with Beinn a' Chroin.

Ben Vorlich.credit: Grinner at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0
Ben Vorlich.about: A neat pointed summit with a trig point above Loch Earn, and one of the great viewpoints of the southern Highlands.

routes.name: Ardvorlich
routes.text: From Ardvorlich on the south shore of Loch Earn, up Glen Vorlich on a track, then the clear north ridge path.

routes.name: With Stùc a' Chroin
routes.text: Down the south-west ridge to the Bealach an Dubh Choirein and up Stùc a' Chroin.

Beinn Dubhchraig.about: A broad hill rising above the Caledonian pinewood of Coille Coire Chuilc, west of Tyndrum.

routes.name: Dalrigh
routes.text: Through the pinewood and up beside the Allt Coire Dubhchraig to the north-east ridge. Usually combined with Ben Oss.

Stùc a' Chroin.about: Ben Vorlich's craggy neighbour, guarded on the north by a steep buttress.

routes.name: Over Ben Vorlich
routes.text: From Ardvorlich over Ben Vorlich to the Bealach an Dubh Choirein, then steep rough paths with scrambling up the right side of the buttress.

routes.name: Glen Ample and Beinn Each
routes.text: From Ardchullarie on Loch Lubnaig, the forest path to the head of Glen Ample, over Beinn Each and along a very rough, rocky ridge.
